- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) mid-history, model often lags in correction; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak unless sentiment sustains.
- If news volume drops below 2.0 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.3–0.8% per day of low volume.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast deviates >1.5% from 14d moving average, revert toward it by 0.1–0.3% per day.
- When sentiment change is negative and cumulative, model often underreacts; add 0.2–0.5% to forecast to compensate for lag.
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.33 or more in 3 consecutive days), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 5 values.
